note: XVII grounds, statues and rooftops (Ian, 17 Nov).
style: A cinematic Romantic oil painting of 1893 in the manner of the reference: academic realism, atmospheric haze, rich colour and light, a wide establishing view, painterly brushwork. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Exterior, the formal grounds of a Victorian asylum in autumn 1893: a weathered marble statue of a robed woman on a plinth beside clipped yew hedges, a manicured lawn and gravel walk leading to the long house, fallen leaves, grey afternoon light. Any people are small and far off, with no detail in their faces.

Exterior: a stone terrace with balustrade and carved stone urns overlooking a sweeping manicured lawn and the cedar trees of an asylum park, 1893, soft late-afternoon light breaking through cloud. Any people are small and far off, with no detail in their faces.

Exterior: an avenue of clipped topiary yews and box hedges in the asylum garden at dusk, a gardener small with a wheelbarrow, the lit windows of the house at the end of the walk. Any people are small and far off, with no detail in their faces.

Exterior: a still round stone fountain basin with a mossy cherub in the centre of a formal lawn at dusk, reflecting the pale sky, the dark house and its chimneys behind. Any people are small and far off, with no detail in their faces.
Exterior, on the leads of the asylum roof at sunset, 1893: tall chimney stacks, slate slopes and a stone parapet, the wide view beyond over the Thames and the marshes glowing red and gold. No people.

Exterior at night: a marble statue of an angel in the asylum garden, silvered by moonlight against black trees, a lit study window far behind it across the lawn. Any people are small and far off, with no detail in their faces.
